newsitem.title: BRAZIL: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN RECOVERS FROM MISHAP TO WIN ON LAST LAP.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN RECOVERS FROM MISHAP TO WIN ON LAST LAP.

text.p: World motorcycling champion Michael Doohan recovered from a mistake when he skidded onto the grass to claim a dramatic last-lap win in the Brazilian Grand Prix on Sunday.

Doohan, who wrapped up this year's 500cc championship in Catalonia last month to win his third successive title, appeared to be out of contention when he was distracted by a backmarker and went onto the grass.

But the Australian, who made it clear he would not use the trip simply as an excuse to savour the delights of Rio, made up lost ground and overtook leader Alex Criville on the last lap after the Spaniard appeared to lose concentration.
In the 250cc category, Italy's Max Biaggi, who needed to finish 11th or higher to clinch the world title, missed his chance for glory by crashing out in the early stages of the race.

Doohan, riding a Honda, was second behind Japan's Norifumi Abe when the two caught up with Japan's Toshi Arakaki in the 18th lap. Both were overtaken by Criville as they became entangled with the backmarker, much to Doohan's disgust.
"It amazes me how Arakaki gets a ride. He shouldn't be in a national race let alone out here," he said.
"Abe managed to slow up in time but I felt I was going to hit him and had to do a bit of grass tracking. I'm glad it wasn't wet out there."
Doohan overtook Abe two laps later, caught up with Criville, another Honda man, with two laps remaining and sped past him in a thrilling final lap to win by 0.465 seconds.
"I just put my head down and went for it. He (Criville) made a few mistakes and I managed to take advantage," Doohan said.
Criville, denied what would have been his third win of the season, said: "I became a bit nervous and I began to make mistakes. I need more experience in this sort of situation."
Doohan, whose win was his eighth of the season and his first in Brazil, said before the race that he would not relax, even though he had the championship in the bag.
He began in pole position and led for the first two thirds of the race but was always under pressure from Abe, riding a Yamaha. Abe eventually finished third.
Germany's Ralf Waldmann finished second in the 250cc to slash Biaggi's lead in the championship to one point.

Biaggi was sixth on the grid, fought his way up to second but then crashed out as he attempted to overtake Jurgen Fuchs. His team said he suffered a cut on his chin but would be able to race in Australia.
The race was won by Frenchman Olivier Jacque on a Honda, who claimed his first-ever Grand Prix win.
Japan's Haruchika Aomi, riding a Honda, won the 125cc race to move within a hair's breadth of winning his second consecutive title in the category.

Aoki, who leads despite having previously won only one race this season, had a comfortable win while his compatriot Masaki Tokudome, second in the world championship, finished third on the track where he last year claimed his first grand prix win.
Tokudome trails by 23 points and can only take the title if he wins in Australia and Aoki fails to earn a point.
